The decision sum
mary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every\nclient reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating

on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
 counts are case-execution *variants*, wit
h iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a differen
t total under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is nev

er converted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is
 the authori
ty and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial i
n it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a f
ailure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.r
eason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete`
says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n

"nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids,
prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you ca

n append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`a
nthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-yo
ur-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `d

etails.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns
the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`)
. Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.reas

on: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints)
is launchable only through a suite that has\nit **attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{s
uiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId
` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT

_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depe
hed → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400`

with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — in
cluding the servers its\npinned plugin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`40
0`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nf

or a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run i
s pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLIC

T` (409)
rather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{pr

ojectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite,
`POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and o
ptional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments
, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the ba
ckend supplies the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }`
when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The na
me is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching
process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case sna
pshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run records which environment it used. `GET .../ev
al-runs/{runId}` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, n

ot the suite's current attachments — or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is
capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns\n`429` with `details.reason: \"CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT\"` — wait for an

active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` h
andles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accou

nts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and
refresh it server-side when you stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effort

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing
field. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `so
urce`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is\naccepted e

verywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `s
et.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST ...
/ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`
, read back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`,
